line.sato_kei.again4.1: Evenings Misha and I work on an old radio. So far it gets one station, and that one is about the weather.
line.sato_kei.sun_low.1: I don't measure sunsets. I tried once, and it felt awkward, as if I were peeking.
line.sato_kei.sun_night.1: At night the instruments rest. I still look west, where it went.
line.sato_mila.again2.1: At the clinic today everyone had the same thing: October, a runny nose, not enough sleep. The prescription's the same too: tea and bed.
line.sato_mila.again3.2: I do. That's why in the evening I go down to the sea and for ten minutes I treat nobody.
line.sato_mila.again4.1: Yuki wants to be a doctor. Yesterday she cured a toy rabbit and prescribed me an ice cream.
line.sato_mila.sun_day.1: It's sunny today, and the clinic is quiet. Even the queue isn't in a hurry, everyone's sitting by the window.
line.sato_mila.sun_low.1: When the sun goes down, Yuki pulls me straight to the window. We're both like that, I don't know who we get it from.
line.sato_yuki.again2.1: Sonya and I are building a little house for beetles on the bench. No beetles have moved in yet.
line.sato_yuki.again3.3: Papa is ticklish. Really, really ticklish. Don't tell anyone.
line.sato_yuki.again4.1: Mum said if I eat my porridge I'll grow right up to the ceiling. I'm eating it, but the ceiling's still far away.
line.sato_yuki.sun_day.1: I shut my eyes in the sunshine and it was still all red. You can see the sun even through your eyes.
line.sato_yuki.sun_low.1: Look how long my shadow is. Like a grown-up's. The sun does that.
line.korneev_ivan.again2.1: Nina says I'm all thumbs. Fifty years she's been saying it. And who fixed the kitchen tap yesterday?
line.korneev_ivan.again3.2: Flounder. And the flounder fishes for my patience. So far she's ahead.
line.korneev_ivan.again4.1: At the Laboratory it's all computers now. In my day the main instrument was a file. And a head.
line.korneev_ivan.sun_low.1: At dawn from the shore you can see the light coming to you across the water. Right to your feet. Every morning, and I still can't get used to it.
line.korneev_ivan.sun_day.1: Sit a while. Sun on your back, no wind. A man needs nothing more.
line.korneeva_nina.again2.1: Galina Zotova came to me to learn to salt cabbage. A chemist, and she's afraid to add salt by eye.
line.korneeva_nina.again2.2: I tell her: Galya, salt isn't a reagent, you feel it.
line.hero.korneeva_nina_again3.1: Do you really know everyone here?
line.korneeva_nina.again3.2: Everyone. And who gets up when. Vanya, for one, at six, and he knocks his rod against the door.
line.korneeva_nina.again4.1: It gets dark early in October, and I still sit on the bench till the last minute. At home there's the television, out here there are people.
line.korneeva_nina.sun_day.1: Sit in the sun with me. For old bones the sun's the best medicine, Mila Sato will tell you.
line.korneeva_nina.sun_low.1: The sun's moved round to the house opposite. I think I'll move to that bench, after it.
line.belov_misha.again2.1: Bought a soldering station in town. Now I solder at home, and the neighbours think I'm cooking something weird.
line.belov_misha.again3.1: I'm fixing Rustam's kettle. An engineer, and kettles beat him. He says they're not his scale.
line.belov_misha.again4.1: Weekends I take a thermos up to the lookout. You sit, you look, and your head cools down by itself.
line.belov_misha.sun_low.1: Tonight's sunset is like the lamp on an old instrument: warm, orange. Means everything's fine.
line.belov_misha.sun_night.1: At night I solder longer and it comes out worse. Seems my hands are waiting for morning too.
line.orlova_tanya.again2.1: The bread comes in by nine. By ten Nina knows what it's like today, and the whole yard knows from Nina.
line.orlova_tanya.again3.1: About twenty people came in today. Five bought something, the rest were warming up.
line.orlova_tanya.again4.1: I take fish by weight, but I remember every one by its face. Especially the gobies: they look offended.
line.orlova_tanya.sun_day.1: The sun's fallen across the counter, right onto the bread. Take that loaf, it isn't warm from the oven.
line.orlova_tanya.sun_cloudy.1: Overcast. On days like this everyone buys more than they need. Filling some gap, I suppose.
line.lange_pyotr.again2.1: At low tide so much sand comes out that the gulls walk about on it like they own it.
line.lange_pyotr.again3.2: In October, yes. But the fish aren't lazy. The cod come in closer.
line.lange_pyotr.again4.1: My father painted the boat. Every spring I paint her the same colour. That way she knows me.
line.lange_pyotr.sun_day.1: By day the sun goes right down to the bottom. The fish go deeper, and I sit and warm my hands.
line.lange_pyotr.sun_low.1: At dawn at sea the first thing you do is look east. Not for the weather. You just look.
line.kimura_dasha.again2.1: Tomorrow's the optics colloquium. I've learned everything except what they'll ask.
line.kimura_dasha.again3.2: Rocks, gulls and quiet. I read my notes aloud there, and nobody tells me off.
line.kimura_dasha.again4.1: Vika left another note on the fridge: "Buy bread, don't buy biscuits." I always misread the second half.
line.kimura_dasha.sun_low.1: At sunset I count the seconds while it slips below the horizon. No idea why. I just don't want to miss it.
line.kimura_dasha.sun_night.1: At night I study physics, and I know from a formula where the sun is right now. Somehow that doesn't make it easier.
line.li_vika.again2.1: Washing flasks today I found a note in one: "Vika, you're the best." Zotov's handwriting. Or Galina's. I'm not going to ask.
line.li_vika.again3.1: My favourite is the minute when everything's washed and nobody has had time to dirty anything yet.
line.li_vika.again4.1: Dasha talks in formulas in her sleep. Last night she said "negligibly small" and smiled.
line.li_vika.sun_night.1: I come home from the Laboratory in the dark now. October steals a little more of the sun from me every day.
line.li_vika.sun_cloudy.1: Overcast. The flasks don't shine in the light, and washing them feels like it's for nobody.
line.valiev_rustam.again2.1: I replaced the bulb on our stairs. Nobody asked, but it was flickering at a frequency I did not like.
line.valiev_rustam.again3.2: A test rig. First I said it could not be done. Now we are at the "we'll see" stage.
line.valiev_rustam.again4.1: Zotov has offered me a game of correspondence chess. Through the wall: our offices are next door.
line.valiev_rustam.sun_low.1: In the evening the light comes in almost level and shows every bump in the wall. No spirit level can do that.
line.valiev_rustam.sun_night.1: It is dark. The window has turned into a mirror, and there is only me in it. In the day there was more world in it.
line.nishimura_aya.again2.1: I've run out of ultramarine, and they don't sell it in town. I'm painting the sea in ochre. It seems almost glad.
line.nishimura_aya.again3.2: Look. Just don't say it's a good likeness. A camera does likenesses.
line.nishimura_aya.again4.1: I draw people in the yard while they aren't looking. Only Sorokin always notices, and sits still.
line.nishimura_aya.sun_low.1: This is the best hour. Everything's golden, even the bin. I'd paint only in this hour, but it's short.
line.nishimura_aya.sun_day.1: By day on the island the sun stands behind my shoulder. I don't paint it. It watches me paint.
line.sorokin_oleg.again2.1: The swallows left back in September. Every year I write down the date, and every year I'm a little offended.
line.sorokin_oleg.again3.2: From eight in the morning. Bench, thermos, binoculars. I believe the tits took me for part of the bench long ago.
line.sorokin_oleg.again4.1: This morning a flock of starlings went over the houses, three hundred or so. I counted, lost count, and don't regret it in the least.
line.sorokin_oleg.sun_day.1: The sun has reached the bench. The birds notice it before I do, and I notice the birds.
line.sorokin_oleg.sun_cloudy.1: Overcast. On days like this the birds sing more quietly, and I don't quite know what I'm waiting for.
line.khuazhev_aslan.again2.1: My mother called. Asked whether I've got thin. I said no. With cheese this close, how could I?
line.khuazhev_aslan.again3.2: I do, my friend. That is why I sell cheese: every round smells of our yard back home.
line.khuazhev_aslan.again4.1: Evenings the young folk gather by the club. They don't buy cheese, but they laugh well. That gladdens me too.
line.khuazhev_aslan.sun_day.1: Sun on the tent, and the cheese turns golden under it. Customers think I laid it out that nicely myself.
line.khuazhev_aslan.sun_night.1: Dark now, but the tent is still holding the day's warmth. I sit in it as if in a felt cloak.
line.guseva_valentina.again2.1: I'm closing up the dacha any day now. These are the last cobs, and after that it's just pickles till spring.
line.guseva_valentina.again3.2: Every day. The pot gets bored without me, and I get bored without people.
line.guseva_valentina.again4.1: Nina Korneeva drops by every day. Doesn't take corn, she's minding her teeth. Brings the news instead.
line.guseva_valentina.sun_day.1: In the sun the steam over the pot glows all over. That's what people walk towards, though they think it's the corn.
line.guseva_valentina.sun_cloudy.1: Overcast. On a day like this even the corn is only yellow for form's sake.
line.kid_girl.book_bird_tail.1: Oh. You've got a crest and a yellow tail. You're not a sparrow. You must have come out of a book.
line.kimura_dasha.no_column_yet.1: A crest, red drops on the wings. There's no column for you in my table. Sit still, I'll start a new one.
line.sato_yuki.grandpa_bench.1: Birdie, you want Grandpa Sorokin. That's his bench, the next one. He's been looking for birds like you his whole life.
line.sato_yuki.jam_drops.1: Who are you? You've got a little tuft, a yellow tail and red drops on your wings, like jam.
line.lange_pyotr.olegs_bird.1: Never seen your like at sea. You'll be Oleg's, then. Fly to the Academgorodok, he's waiting.
line.belov_misha.unknown_marking.1: Red marks on the wings, a yellow one on the tail. I don't know this marking. Go and show yourself to Sorokin, he reads diagrams like you.
line.nishimura_aya.cadmium_tail.1: Stay. Pinkish grey, cadmium yellow at the tip of the tail, crimson lake on the wings. Sorokin will see you, on paper at least.
line.zotova_galina.next_bench_longer.1: It is not me you want, it is the next bench, Sorokin's. He has been waiting for you longer than I have worked at the Laboratory.
line.zotova_galina.reagent_wax.1: That red on the wings is exactly the sealing wax on old reagent bottles. You are not from here, that much is clear without a guide.
line.zotov_lev.not_imagined.1: The next bench, Sorokin. He has waited forty years for this observation. Do not make him write down "imagined it".
line.zotov_lev.handsome_error.1: Nothing like you is on record in our yard. If you are an observational error, you are a very handsome one.
line.korneeva_nina.ears_off_yard.1: Off you go to Sorokin, to Oleg. That's his bench, the next one. He's talked the whole yard's ears off about you, let him see you for himself for once.
line.korneeva_nina.postcard_bird.1: Goodness, a crest. I've only ever seen a bird like you on a postcard. Tanya won't believe me.
line.korneev_ivan.olegs_department.1: Look at that, a crest. Never seen one like you in my life, and I've lived a fair while. Fly to Oleg, you're his department.
line.valiev_rustam.data_sheet.1: A crest, a yellow edge on the tail. I don't know this model. Show yourself to Sorokin, he's bound to have your data sheet.
line.guseva_valentina.two_steps_bench.1: Not to me, not to me. Sorokin's bench is two steps away, he's waited all his life for one like you. Go to him.
line.guseva_valentina.corn_butter_tail.1: Look at you, a crest, and the tail as if it had been dipped in the corn butter. I've never had one like you at my cart.
line.khuazhev_aslan.wedding_guest.1: Now that is a guest. A crest, little red buttons on the wings, dressed as if for a wedding. We never saw one like you back in the mountains.
line.nao.ice_in_glass.1: You're not from here. Your voice is like ice in a glass. Someone must be waiting for you very much.
line.guy_b.alarm_to_the_end.1: Who's ringing in here? A bird with a crest, in the club. A trill like an alarm clock you actually want to hear to the end.
line.clerk.precious_cells.1: Don't move. The red drops on your wings are exactly one cell each. The most precious cells on the whole sheet.
line.guseva_valentina.sorokin_many_words: Sorokin tells everyone about his bird now. He's told me three times. I never knew the man had so many words in him.
line.korneeva_nina.jumped_like_young.1: Valya says Sorokin jumped up off his bench like a young man. With those knees of his. Shame I was in the grocery.
line.korneev_ivan.margin_bird.1: Oleg drew his bird for me in the margin of the paper, next to the chess problem. Nina grumbles, but I'm not rubbing it out.
line.sato_yuki.one_long_word.1: Grandpa Sorokin showed me a page in his journal. I could only read one word, a long one: "waxwing".
line.nishimura_aya.crest_grows.1: Sorokin asked me to paint his waxwing from memory. Not mine, his. Second sheet now, and with every telling the crest gets taller.
line.zotova_galina.binocular_honour.1: Sorokin let Lev look through his binoculars. Offered them himself. Lev says it's a great honour, and I say it's euphoria.
line.kimura_dasha.rare_column.1: Sorokin asked me to add a "rare" column to my table. So far it has one row, and he filled it in himself.
line.belov_misha.bigger_feeder.1: Sorokin ordered a bigger feeder from me, in case the others turn up. There's nothing to solder in it, but I said yes.
journal.heard.tanya_rowan_doorway: Tanya at the grocery says I have a face like Sorokin's. I don't know if that's a compliment.
journal.heard.olya_north_send_off: Olya saw me off to the north: if I see a waxwing, Sorokin first, then her. Now I only have to see one.
journal.heard.dasha_tally_stump: A student from the benches said she can't sit like a stump even in an exam. It turns out I can.
journal.heard.sorokin_views_small_town: Sorokin heard from Aya that I looked at the town from the rowan wood, and said that from a bird's height every town is small. He would know.
journal.heard.nina_cob_for_vanya: Nina smelled the cob in my pocket from across the yard and told me to tell Ivan to share. I'll pass it on, but I promise nothing.
journal.heard.lange_crows_crate: The fisherman on the promenade asked me to tell the crows he sees everything: they steal herring from his crate. I passed it on with a handful of feed.
journal.heard.yuki_crows_from_bench: Yuki watches the crows from her bench and knows the one that took her button. I can't tell them apart yet.
journal.heard.misha_rustam_window: Rustam's bench neighbour asked whether I was the signal Rustam has been waiting for all evening. Not yet.
journal.heard.vika_pigeon_twice: Vika asked me to put the pigeon down twice. Science, in her view, should be fair to pigeons too.
journal.heard.lev_soda_eyes_shut: Lev Zotov claims he can tell Baikal from Tarragon with his eyes shut. He asked me not to tell Galina, so he isn't sure himself.
journal.heard.galina_interferometer: Galina knows about the magazine under the interferometer and thinks the leg could simply have been filed down. I won't pass that on to Lev.
journal.heard.valentina_aslan_sent: Valentina says Aslan praises her corn without ever having tried it, and told me to eat for two. I'm doing my best.
journal.heard.nao_supper_smoke: Nao at the door says the tent smells of smoke, like a campfire that isn't there. Now I notice it too.
journal.heard.aslan_braid_fisher: Aslan guessed at once that the braid was for a fisherman: fishermen take the smoked kind so that something isn't fish. Lange wouldn't argue.
journal.heard.clerk_soda_palette: Yamada at the next computer named the four sodas by their colours and called it a good palette. Now that's how I remember them.
journal.heard.owner_lamp_batteries: The owner sold me the lamp and said this light may be touched: it runs on batteries. I didn't ask about the other light.
journal.heard.timur_owner_ate: Timur saw the owner eating cheese at the booth window and watched it like a film. So I wasn't the only one waiting for that.
journal.heard.vera_sparrow_retold: Vera, Sonya's mum, leaves her program to hear the sparrow story to the end. It's good to be heard out.
journal.heard.tyoma_sparrow_no_hello: Tyoma told Sonya sparrows don't say hello, and now she doesn't say hello to him. The sparrow is not to blame, but I feel a little awkward.
journal.heard.olya_aya_atlas: Aya borrowed the atlas of the area from the library to find where I stood. I don't remember exactly myself, so I hope she finds a better spot.
journal.heard.tanya_rowan_again: Tanya says Sorokin bought dried rowan again, in case the others find the way too. It's a long way; I know.
journal.heard.nao_aslan_pancakes: Aslan tells even Nao about the pancakes with sour cream, though she only stands at the door. Every piece of news seems to come through that door.
journal.heard.lev_soda_mixed_up: Lev admitted he might mix up Duchesse and Buratino, and Galina is already bringing four glasses. I said nothing.
journal.heard.kei_soup_measured: Kei Sato is pleased the independent expert sided with him: fish soup, like light, has to be measured yourself. I measured it with a spoon.
journal.heard.misha_two_lamps: Rustam wants to repeat the experiment with two lamps, and his bench neighbour will hold the second. Science in the Academgorodok is growing.
journal.heard.vika_dishes_traitors: Vika is doing the dishes and calls the pigeons traitors: they never came to my feeder. Honestly, I didn't talk them out of it.
journal.heard.sorokin_magpie_faces: Sorokin approves of Misha apologising to the magpie: magpies remember faces longer than people do. I hope it remembers mine for a good reason.
journal.heard.valentina_cheese_salt: Aslan sent Valentina a round of cheese for the salt, and she understood I had told him the truth about her corn. I had.
journal.heard.ivan_cheese_for_petya: Ivan says nobody has brought Lange anything for twenty years. One cheese braid isn't much for twenty years, but it's a start.
journal.heard.nina_yuki_crows: Nina says Yuki talks to the crows now the way Nina talks to Tanya. That is, at length and about everything.
journal.heard.clerk_screensaver_still: The man at the next computer said I sat so still he took me for a screensaver. He didn't say for how long.
journal.heard.sonya_ask_owner_sun: The girl at the iMac asked me to ask the owner whether the sun is out there: he always knows. I didn't understand where 'there' was.
journal.heard.nika_soda_bets: The girl who keeps talking to her screen told her chat I was heading for the machine and took bets. I don't know who won.
journal.heard.nao_pigeons_no_hurry: The girl at the club door says pigeons come to those who aren't in a hurry. I have nowhere to hurry to, so my chances are good.
journal.heard.nao_cliff_from_below: The girl at the club door asked me to go down to the beach and see how it all looks from below. She has only seen it from above.
journal.heard.owner_whole_town_below: The owner said there's a whole town below and I should walk round it slowly. I still have time, he says.
journal.heard.timur_polar_for_the_wood: Timur told me the cable car runs to Polar Star, and the old wood is a stone's throw from there. Not every road north has to be walked.
journal.heard.owner_news_like_draught: The owner already knew I'd gone north after a bird: news passes his booth like a draught. He said it was good I came back.
journal.heard.nika_punk_crest_picture: Nika asked whether the waxwing really has a crest like a punk's: someone sent her a picture. It does, only neater.
journal.heard.vera_yellow_tip_asked: Sonya asked her mum whether the waxwing's tail tip really looks dipped in paint. Vera told her to ask someone who has seen one, which means me.
journal.heard.nao_fireworks_small: Nao says the fireworks will look small from up here and told me to go down and see the big ones. She'll watch from above.
journal.heard.owner_cheerful_thunder: Under the hill the fireworks sound like distant thunder, only cheerful, the owner said. He heard them and I saw them, so between us we had the whole thing.
journal.heard.lange_wish_not_fish: The fisherman on the promenade said I may wish for anything but fish: fish he can manage himself. That I can do.
journal.heard.aslan_blini_with_cheese: Aslan recommends at least one pancake with cheese at Maslenitsa: cheese, he says, is milk too, only patient. I like that word.
journal.heard.nao_one_lantern_faster: Nao saw one lantern rise faster than the rest and decided it was mine. I lost sight of mine, so I won't argue.
journal.heard.sonya_stayed_up_almost: Sonya was allowed to stay up for the fireworks, and she did. Almost.
journal.heard.nika_wish_three_viewers: Nika asks me to wish her at least three viewers on a shooting star. A modest wish; I can spare one.
journal.heard.timur_sunrise_slept_warm: Timur slept through the sunrise but woke up warm, as if he'd been on the shore too. Maybe that counts.
journal.heard.olya_wish_third_draft: Olya is on her third draft of her wish for the bamboo. I hung mine on the first try, and now I'm a little worried.
journal.heard.valentina_sorokin_words: Valentina has heard about Sorokin's bird three times already. She never knew he had so many words in him; neither did I.
journal.heard.nina_jumped_like_young: Nina is sorry she was at the grocery when Sorokin jumped up from his bench like a young man. I was not far off, but I keep quiet about it.
journal.heard.ivan_margin_bird: Sorokin drew his bird for Ivan in the margin of the paper, next to the chess problem. Nina scolds, Ivan won't rub it out, and he's right.
journal.heard.yuki_one_long_word: Yuki could make out only one word in Sorokin's journal, the long one: waxwing. She read the part that matters.
journal.heard.aya_crest_grows: Aya is drawing the waxwing from Sorokin's memory, and with every telling the crest gets taller. I remember what it was really like, but let it grow.
journal.heard.galina_binocular_honour: Sorokin let Lev look through his binoculars without being asked. Lev calls it an honour, Galina calls it euphoria, and I think it's the same thing.
journal.heard.dasha_rare_column: Dasha's table has a new column, 'rare'. It has one line, and Sorokin wrote it in himself, in his small, even hand.
journal.heard.misha_bigger_feeder: Sorokin has ordered a bigger feeder from Misha, in case the others come. They probably won't, but let the feeder be there.
journal.heard.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_seen: Sorokin said 'well, hello' the way you say it to someone you've waited forty years for. I sat beside him and tried not to move.
journal.heard.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_again: Sorokin again invited the waxwing to sit closer: he doesn't bite, he said. I sat closer.
journal.heard.sorokin_oleg.namesake_magp: Sorokin greets magpies as namesakes: he borrowed his surname from them and still hasn't given it back. I heard it from the back of his bench.
journal.heard.sorokin_oleg.bird_visit: Sorokin greets any bird with 'not a waxwing, but good all the same'. I don't think you could say anything better about anyone.
journal.heard.kid_girl.sparrow_seen: Sonya asked for one thing only: not to fly away straight off. I stayed as long as I could.
journal.heard.kid_girl.sparrow_other: Sonya politely explained to a bird that it was pretty, but the deal was about a sparrow. There's no arguing with Sonya.
journal.heard.kid_girl.kuzya_no_tea: Sonya calls her sparrow Kuzya and worries she has nothing to offer a guest, not even tea. I think Kuzya is happy with the invitation.
journal.heard.kid_girl.book_bird_tail: Sonya decided that a bird with a crest and a yellow tail had flown out of a book. I didn't try to talk her out of it.
journal.heard.kid_girl.pigeon_hello_test: Sonya says hello to pigeons too, as a test. Science doesn't stand still in the club either.
journal.heard.kimura_dasha.tit_row_monda: Dasha told a great tit it has been in her table since Monday. It's nice to have been counted for a while.
journal.heard.kimura_dasha.no_column_yet: Dasha said there's no column for a waxwing in her table and promised to start a new one. A whole column for one waxwing.
journal.heard.sato_yuki.crow_soon_fed: Yuki told a hooded crow it would be fed soon, and that she knew by whom. So do I.
journal.heard.sato_yuki.button_suits_you: Yuki told a hooded crow it could keep the button: it suits the crow better. So they've made peace.
journal.heard.sato_yuki.grandpa_bench: Yuki was the first to understand where I needed to go: to Grandpa Sorokin, on the next bench.
journal.heard.sato_yuki.jam_drops: Yuki says the red drops on a waxwing's wings look like jam. Now I see them that way too.
journal.heard.sato_yuki.not_too_close: Yuki isn't afraid of birds, she only asks them not to come too close. I didn't.
journal.heard.lange_pyotr.gull_try_pier: The fisherman on the promenade sent a gull to the pier, to the lad with the rod, in case he gets lucky. Fishermen root for each other, it turns out.
journal.heard.lange_pyotr.olegs_bird: The fisherman on the promenade decided at once that the waxwing was Oleg's and told it to fly to the Academgorodok. So Oleg is Sorokin.
journal.heard.lange_pyotr.counting_meshe: The fisherman lets you sit by him as long as you keep quiet: he's counting meshes. Keeping quiet next to him is easy.
journal.heard.belov_misha.key_under_shir: Misha wears the key on a string under his shirt and asks magpies not to look at him like that. They look anyway.
journal.heard.belov_misha.confess_magpie: Misha questioned a magpie about the key and said he has an investigator. The investigator, by all accounts, is me.
journal.heard.belov_misha.unknown_markin: To Misha a waxwing is an unfamiliar marking: red marks, a yellow one on the tail. He said to show it to Sorokin, who reads diagrams like that.
journal.heard.nishimura_aya.starling_mes: Aya told a starling it would see the town before her messenger did. The messenger hasn't taken offence yet.
journal.heard.nishimura_aya.cadmium_tail: Aya wrote the waxwing down in paints: pinkish grey, cadmium yellow, crimson lake. She'll show it to Sorokin on paper, at least.
journal.heard.nishimura_aya.head_to_the_: Aya asked for the head a little to the left and said thank you. Sitting for a portrait turned out to be easy.
journal.heard.zotova_galina.next_bench_l: Galina is formal even with a bird: she sent it on to the next bench, to Sorokin, who has waited longer than she has worked at the Laboratory.
journal.heard.zotova_galina.reagent_wax: Galina says the red on a waxwing's wings is exactly the sealing wax on old reagent bottles. Chemists have their own way of seeing birds.
journal.heard.zotova_galina.four_bottles: Galina asked a bird not to distract the young man with four bottles: he's working for science. I wasn't distracted.
journal.heard.zotova_galina.no_bread_cro: Galina apologised to a bird for having no bread on her, only a crossword. A crossword isn't bad either.
journal.heard.zotov_lev.rook_referee: Lev told a rook he had already sent his letter to the editors, so there was no need to stare. Rooks do look stern.
journal.heard.zotov_lev.not_imagined: Lev asked that Sorokin not be made to write down 'imagined it'. I did my best so that he wouldn't think he had.
journal.heard.zotov_lev.handsome_error: Lev told a waxwing that if it was an observational error, it was a very handsome one. Being a handsome error isn't so bad.
journal.heard.zotov_lev.came_first: Lev came to the bench first today, and nobody saw. Now I have, and I'm writing it down.
journal.heard.korneeva_nina.pigeon_from_: Nina asked a pigeon whether it had seen a boy with a paper at the fair. So she's waiting.
journal.heard.korneeva_nina.ears_off_yar: Nina says Sorokin has talked the whole yard's ears off about the waxwing, so let him see it for himself for once. I agreed with her.
journal.heard.korneeva_nina.postcard_bir: Nina has only ever seen a bird like that on a postcard and is sure Tanya won't believe her. I think Tanya will.
journal.heard.korneeva_nina.tell_me_prop: Nina asks birds to come down and tell her properly what's going on down there. From above, honestly, everything looks calmer than she thinks.
journal.heard.korneev_ivan.cob_finished: Ivan told a pigeon he finished the corn the same day, to the last kernel. Valentina will be pleased.
journal.heard.korneev_ivan.olegs_departm: Ivan has lived a fair while and never seen a crested bird like that, so he sent it to Oleg, as his department. In this yard everything leads to Sorokin.
journal.heard.korneev_ivan.good_company: Ivan has no crumbs, but good company, he says. It really is nice to sit with him.
journal.heard.valiev_rustam.not_the_sign: Rustam spotted a bird over the yard and ruled at once: signal not counted. His experiment is strict.
journal.heard.valiev_rustam.data_sheet: Rustam doesn't know this model: a crest, a yellow edge to the tail. He said to show it to Sorokin, who is bound to have the waxwing's data sheet.
journal.heard.guseva_valentina.hear_you_: Ivan oiled the wheel of Valentina's cart, and now she hears the sparrows instead of the squeak. It has gone quiet by the cart.
journal.heard.guseva_valentina.two_steps: Valentina sent the waxwing on to Sorokin: his bench is two steps away, and he's waited all his life for one like it. Everybody here knows who is waiting for whom.
journal.heard.guseva_valentina.corn_butt: To Valentina the waxwing's tail looks dipped in corn butter. Everyone here has their own waxwing.
journal.heard.khuazhev_aslan.sonya_kuzya: Aslan knows Sonya's sparrow is called Kuzya: she's told everyone. News travels fast at the club door.
journal.heard.khuazhev_aslan.see_my_gues: Aslan asked a passing bird to check whether his guest is finishing his pancakes. The guest is, honestly.
journal.heard.khuazhev_aslan.wedding_gue: Aslan said the waxwing was dressed as if for a wedding, and they never saw one like it in the mountains. The little red buttons on the wings are smart indeed.
journal.heard.nao.palm_pigeon_unhurried: Nao saw the pigeon that ate from my palm and remembered it took its time. She notices more than she says.
journal.heard.nao.ice_in_glass: Nao says a waxwing's voice is like ice in a glass and someone must be waiting for it very much. She guessed right.
journal.heard.nao.whole_sea_from_above: Nao thinks the whole sea can be seen from above and asked to be told later what it's like. Not the whole of it, but nearly.
journal.heard.owner.braid_crumbs: The owner shares the braid crumbs with the sparrows: he eats slowly, there's enough for everyone. So the supper did more than one of us good.
journal.heard.owner.waxwing_from_north: The owner told a waxwing it was from the north: their kind doesn't come here, he'd have felt it. He feels a great deal without leaving his booth.
journal.heard.owner.on_the_threshold: The owner says the threshold is a good place: neither out there nor in here. I thought about that for a long time.
journal.heard.guy_b.pigeon_comes_back: Timur thinks the pigeons come into the club because the new guy fed them from his hand. The new guy, apparently, is me.
journal.heard.guy_b.alarm_to_the_end: Timur compared a waxwing's trill to an alarm clock you want to hear to the end. I don't remember alarm clocks like that, but I believe him.
journal.heard.guy_b.no_hurry_birds: Timur says nobody in the club is in a hurry, not even the birds. I'd noticed.
journal.heard.streamer.waxwing_on_air: Nika showed the waxwing to her chat: the very one everyone's talking about. She turned the camera just in time.
journal.heard.streamer.bird_more_viewers: The moment a bird got into the shot, Nika's chat woke up. Everyone needs birds, it seems, even streams.
journal.heard.clerk.precious_cells: Yamada counted the waxwing in cells: the red drops on the wings, he says, are the most precious cells on the whole sheet.
journal.heard.clerk.twelve_by_twelve: Yamada says the bird is exactly twelve by twelve cells. He counts everything in cells, and the birds don't seem to mind.
line.owner.again5.1: Yamada sometimes brings me a printout of his mountain. I don't understand it. But I keep it in the booth.
line.owner.again6.2: At two in the morning. There's nobody out there then, only the sea. That's enough for me.
line.owner.again7.1: Timur's fallen asleep in his chair again. Don't wake him. He's due at the warehouse by half past seven.
line.clerk.again5.1: Stas asked me to paint him an avatar. Forty by forty cells. I told him it's a week's work. He agreed.
line.clerk.again6.1: I've started an autumn sheet. It needs twenty shades of yellow. Every morning on my way here I pick up one.
line.clerk.again7.1: The owner hangs my printouts in his booth. Upside down. I don't correct him: the mountain is pretty that way too.
line.clerk.sun_low.1: Around this time I always want to add orange to the sheet. My eyes must remember what it's like outside now.
line.clerk.sun_night.1: It's dark out there now. At this hour I always save the file twice. Just in case.
line.streamer.again5.1: Stas comes into my chat and writes "gg" every time I lose. My only regular viewer.
line.streamer.again6.2: From lunchtime till chat falls asleep. Chat falls asleep later than I do.
line.streamer.again7.1: Chat wants to see autumn. I turned the camera on the garland. They said it'll do.
line.streamer.sun_day.1: Chat's quiet in the daytime. Everyone's out in the sun, probably. I'd go too, honestly. Later.
line.streamer.sun_night.1: Night's when I get the most viewers. As if the sun went away and everyone came here instead.
line.streamer.sun_cloudy.1: Chat says it's overcast. I could tell already: my skin feels cold, though it's warm in here.
line.kid_boy.again5.1: Sonya gave me half a chocolate bar. For not yelling at the boss, she said. I did yell, just quietly.
line.kid_boy.again6.2: Yeah. Eight till half one. Then straight here, before somebody takes my seat.
line.kid_boy.again7.1: The soda machine clicks by itself sometimes when nobody's near it. I reckon it's playing too.
line.kid_boy.sun_day.1: The sun's out there now, right? Let it shine, then. I'll look later, it's not going anywhere.
line.kid_boy.sun_low.1: Mornings on my way to school the sun's right in my eyes, really low. I walk half the way with my eyes shut, like on a dark level.
line.kid_boy.sun_night.1: It's dark already, right? I reckon when the sun goes, the Sega plays louder.
line.kid_boy.sun_cloudy.1: It's overcast today, Sonya says. She can tell by her cat: on days like this it doesn't blink.
line.kid_girl.again5.1: Mum's typed four hundred lines already. When her eyes get tired, I read the numbers out to her.
line.kid_girl.again6.2: A little. When he's losing, I'm his friend. When he wins, he shows off.
line.kid_girl.again7.1: Nao at the door says the leaves in the alley are all yellow now. She brings me one every day, and I keep them in my exercise book.
line.kid_girl.sun_low.1: The sun's probably red right now. I'd draw it, but I've only got blue letters.
line.kid_girl.sun_cloudy.1: The sun's hiding today. I hide too sometimes, when I'm tired. Let it rest.
line.guy_a.again5.1: Timur's at the warehouse from the morning, I'm at lectures. And we still only see each other here, though we share a flat.
line.guy_a.again6.1: Yamada's making me an avatar, forty by forty cells. Till then I've got a grey square, and I tell everyone: waiting on the master.
line.guy_a.again7.2: I sleep. One till eight. The rest is lectures and matches, in that order. Sometimes the other way round.
line.guy_a.sun_day.1: No glare on my monitors in the daytime, there aren't any windows. But I still squint sometimes. Habit, I suppose.
line.guy_a.sun_low.1: They say everything's orange outside right now. My second monitor's night mode is the same colour. Practically the same thing.
line.guy_a.sun_night.1: At night the ping's twelve. Everyone's asleep, even the sun. Just me in the lobby.
line.guy_a.sun_cloudy.1: Someone said it's overcast today. I always get kicked on days like that. Not science, experience.
line.guy_b.again5.1: Today at the warehouse we unloaded pumpkins. A whole lorry. Now I know how much autumn weighs.
line.guy_b.again6.1: The owner sometimes keeps tea for me in the booth. He says it's run out, then he finds some. Just for me, I reckon.
line.guy_b.again7.2: Flatmate. And friend. He pays for the electricity, I pay for the internet. He uses more of the internet.
line.guy_b.sun_low.1: Mornings at the warehouse a beam comes straight in through the gates and lies across the whole floor. We all stop. Nobody ever agreed to.
line.guy_b.sun_night.1: At night the ventilation hums quieter. Or maybe I just hear it that way, because I know the sun's down.
line.girl_a.again5.1: Sonya told me she likes waiting. I don't know whether to praise her for it or worry.
line.girl_a.again6.1: At work I'm with instruments all day, and in the evening I come here to the Spectrum. Olya says I rest from machines with a machine.
line.girl_a.again7.2: I don't know. The magazine ended at line four hundred and twelve, but the program didn't.
line.girl_a.sun_day.1: At the lab I sit by the window. The sun creeps across my desk, and I can tell the time by it better than by the clock.
line.girl_a.sun_low.1: In winter, by the end of my shift, the sun comes through the lab window straight into your eyes. I lower the blinds halfway. All the way would be a shame.
line.girl_a.sun_night.1: There's no sun now, but the Spectrum is warm as a stove. I warm my hands on it while it finishes counting.
line.girl_a.sun_cloudy.1: Overcast, they say. On days like this I make more mistakes in the lines. Silly, but I keep a note of it.
line.girl_b.again5.1: Wednesdays the library's empty. I read whatever was returned last. That's how I know what the whole Academgorodok is thinking about.
line.hero.girl_b_again6.1: Are you here every day too?
line.girl_b.again6.2: After the library. Nika keeps the seat next to her for me, but I still sit in mine. Number eight.
line.girl_b.again7.1: Vera asks me to print out every Spectrum program on the forum. I print them. Not one matches her magazine.
line.girl_b.sun_low.1: The forum has a thread: where people saw the sun right down by the ground. Someone posts every day. I read all of it.
line.girl_b.sun_night.1: At night fewer people post on the forum. As if everyone's waiting for it to be light again and saving their words.
line.girl_b.sun_cloudy.1: Overcast. On days like this three new threads about the sun go up on the forum at once. And not one of them gets a reply.
line.nao.again5.1: From here I see everyone who comes out. Timur walks out fast, and Yamada always looks back at the door.
line.nao.again6.2: A little. In autumn the wind off the sea comes right up to the door. But inside I'm colder.
line.nao.again7.1: Olya brings me books from the library. I read a page and look at the alley. That way one book lasts a week.
line.lange_pyotr.cheese_smoked_pocket.1: Twenty years of fish. And you smell of smoke. A braid?
line.lange_pyotr.cheese_smoked_pocket.2: That's just what I need. Give it here and I won't forget it.
line.lange_pyotr.cheese_low_sun.1: Sun's low. The tent by the club is open ten till eight, shut on Mondays. A smoked braid.
line.lange_pyotr.cheese_clouds.1: Clouds. Fish get bolder under clouds, and here I am without cheese. The braid, by the club.
line.li_vika.lunch_after_dark.1: It's dark already and you haven't eaten. Neither have I, but I'm used to it. The Chaika by the lower station is open in the evening, go.
line.li_vika.lunch_raw_herring.1: You smell of fish. That isn't soup, that's raw material. The soup is made at the diner across from the lower station.
line.li_vika.lunch_corn_courier.1: They say you took Korneev his corn too. Everyone in this yard eats lunch now, except me.
line.owner.supper_night_hurry.1: The sun's set, I can feel it. Aslan by the door sells till eight, but the Baikal in the machine never sleeps.
line.owner.supper_soda_first.1: I see the Baikal. Now the braid, from Aslan's tent by the door.
line.owner.supper_braid_first.1: I can smell the braid from here. Now a Baikal from the machine, here in the hall.
line.girl_b.overdue_dark_bench.1: It's dark already. Lev sits on a bench in the yard till seven, if he hasn't frozen. If you miss him, ask tomorrow.
line.girl_b.overdue_cloudy_quiet.1: On a grey day the library goes completely quiet. The magazine is in the machine at the station, by the pendulum. Forty rubles, Lev gave you that, didn't he?
line.zotov_lev.shores_too_thin.1: You've got "Shores"? A good magazine. Only thin, it wouldn't do under an interferometer.
line.guseva_valentina.corn_low_sun.1: The sun's low already. Vanya leaves his bench at half past five, so off you go while it's hot.
line.guseva_valentina.corn_paper_known.1: So you're the one who took Nina her paper? She's told everyone. Then here's another job: take a cob to Vanya, her husband.
line.guseva_valentina.corn_paper_known.2: He used to come every day, and now it's the rod from dawn. Buy the cob first, the pot doesn't sell on credit. Come back and we'll settle up.
line.korneev_ivan.corn_angler_news.1: The cob's gone, only the core left. And Petya says you pulled a fish out off his pier?
line.korneev_ivan.corn_angler_news.2: Tell Valya about the salt. The fish I'll tell her about myself, with the measurements.
line.korneeva_nina.petya_smiles.1: So Petya Lange got his cheese? Vanya told me. He says Petya smiles over his nets now, and the fish can't make it out.
journal.heard.nina_petya_smiles: Nina heard from Ivan that Lange smiles over his nets now. The fish are puzzled, she says. So am I, a little.
line.belov_misha.soup_appeal.1: Vika says the independent expert sides with the soup. The expert just likes dill. I'm filing an appeal.
journal.heard.misha_soup_appeal: Misha thinks the independent expert simply likes dill, and he's appealing. I do like dill, to be fair.
line.clerk.supper_papers.1: You're taking him supper? I only ever take him papers. Supper is probably nicer.
journal.heard.yamada_supper_papers: Yamada only ever takes the owner papers, and he thinks supper is nicer. He's probably right.
line.streamer.olya_debt_closed.1: Chat, we have news: Olya closed a reader's debt. It had been hanging for half a year. She's told me everything already, in detail.
journal.heard.nika_olya_debt_closed: Nika announced to her chat that Olya had closed a reader's debt. I don't think she mentioned the interferometer.
line.lange_pyotr.ivan_fibbed.1: Vanya went to Valya's cart. Told her the fish stopped biting. Tells me about it. Me, a fisherman.
journal.heard.lange_ivan_fibbed: Lange knows Ivan fibbed to Valentina about the fish biting. Ivan told him himself, a fisherman. Secrets in this town are kept by the sea.
line.guseva_valentina.lunar_dumplings.1: For the Lunar New Year the whole town ate dumplings. Two people came to me for corn, and even they had dumplings in a bag.
journal.heard.valentina_lunar_dumplings: Valentina says only two people came to her for corn at the Lunar New Year, and they had dumplings. I'd have been the third.
line.orlova_tanya.holi_pink_hands.1: They say people were throwing coloured powder in the park. Afterwards customers came in with pink hands. The money was pink too.
journal.heard.tanya_holi_pink_hands: After the festival of colours, Tanya at the grocery was taking pink money. Mine was clean: I never took it out.
line.lange_pyotr.lantern_in_net.1: After the festival a paper lantern got into my net. With a candle. I let it go again, let it float.
journal.heard.lange_lantern_in_net: Lange found a paper lantern with a candle in his net and let it go on. Maybe it was mine.
line.owner.moon_quiet_hall.1: Did you watch the moon? I can't see it from here. But on evenings like that the hall goes quiet: everyone's on the promenade.
journal.heard.owner_moon_quiet_hall: The owner didn't see the moon, but he noticed the hall was quiet: everyone had gone to the promenade. Except him.
line.lange_pyotr.dawn_every_day.1: They say the whole town met the sunrise on the shore. I meet it nearly every day, in the boat. Fewer people.
journal.heard.lange_dawn_every_day: Lange meets the sunrise nearly every day, in his boat, with fewer people about. I met it once, but with everyone.
line.korneeva_nina.blini_thin.1: I make my own pancakes for Maslenitsa. My Vanya won't eat the fair ones: too thin, he says, like a paper without a chess problem.
journal.heard.nina_blini_thin: Nina makes her own pancakes: Ivan won't eat the fair ones, too thin, like a paper without a chess problem. Ivan measures everything the same way.
line.nao.pigeons_remember.1: The pigeons look round at you now. That means they remember you. It took them a week to remember me.
journal.heard.nao_pigeons_remember: Nao says the pigeons look round at me now, so they remember me. It took them a week with her, and three handfuls with me.
line.kid_girl.pigeons_easy.1: Were you feeding the pigeons by the door? Pigeons always come. A sparrow only comes if it wants to.
journal.heard.sonya_pigeons_easy: Sonya thinks pigeons always come, but a sparrow only if it wants to. I think she knows something of her own about sparrows.
line.kid_boy.soda_advice.1: Get the Buratino. I've tried them all, Buratino's best. Just don't tell Nika, she bet on the Baikal.
journal.heard.tyoma_soda_advice: Tyoma recommends the Buratino and asks me not to tell Nika: she bet on the Baikal. Now I have a secret because of a soda.
line.owner.machine_honest.1: Had your drink? Our machine is old but honest: what you press is what comes out. Not like people.
journal.heard.owner_machine_honest: The owner says our machine is old but honest, not like people. I didn't ask which people.
